found.lens: Nonlinear optics / ultrafast photonics / fiber optics / RF-microwave engineering. The reading diet: Boyd- and Agrawal-style NLO and fiber papers, ultrafast laser papers, Gaussian-beam and focusing-optimization work, polarimetry/ellipsometry, and the RF side (propagation constants, phase noise, S-parameters). Everything below was checked either by direct derivation or by source lookup; the two numbers I was least sure of (the n2 esu conversion and the Boyd-Kleinman optimum) I re-derived and cross-checked rather than trusting memory — my remembered value for the n2 esu factor was wrong by 10^2 and is corrected here.

gaps.name: Transverse beam-size parameterization (spot size, radius vs diameter, Rayleigh range vs confocal parameter)
gaps.what_breaks: Every candidate meaning of a beam 'width' symbol — w at 1/e^2 of intensity, w at 1/e of intensity, w at 1/e of field, FWHM, ISO 11146 d4-sigma diameter — has dimension L, and z_R and b both have dimension L. The generator solve is exactly blind here: no equation becomes dimensionally inconsistent under any substitution. So the tool will happily translate a peak-intensity or focusing-parameter equation between unit systems while the number it is translating means something else than the reader assumes, and it will report a clean bill of dimensional health. This is the single most common silent error in NLO experimental papers, because 'spot size', 'beam radius', 'beam waist', 'beam diameter' and 'spot diameter' are used interchangeably in prose while the equations assume one specific one.
gaps.magnitude: w(1/e^2 intensity) = sqrt(2) * w(1/e intensity), so peak intensity from a given power is off by exactly 2. FWHM = w*sqrt(2 ln 2) = 1.1774 w, so mistaking FWHM for w gives 1.1774^2 = 1.386 in intensity. Radius vs diameter gives exactly 4 in intensity. Confocal parameter b = 2 z_R, so the Boyd-Kleinman optimum focusing condition L/b = 2.84 becomes L/z_R = 5.68; reading b as z_R halves the inferred optimal crystal length or doubles the inferred optimal waist area.
gaps.example: Peak on-axis intensity of a CW Gaussian beam of power P. Variant A (1/e^2 intensity radius w0, the ISO/laser-industry default, I(r) = I0 exp(-2 r^2 / w0^2)): I0 = 2P/(pi w0^2), and z_R = pi w0^2 / lambda. Variant B (1/e intensity radius w0, common in older plasma/atomic-beam and some spectroscopy papers, I(r) = I0 exp(-r^2 / w0^2)): I0 = P/(pi w0^2). Same symbol, same dimensions, factor 2 in I0. Focusing: Boyd & Kleinman (J. Appl. Phys. 39, 3597 (1968)) optimize xi = L/b with b = 2 z_R = 2 pi w0^2 n / lambda and get xi_opt = 2.84; a paper that writes xi = L/z_R and quotes 2.84 is describing a beam focused twice as tightly.
gaps.fingerprint: Read the Gaussian exponent actually printed in the paper: exp(-2 r^2 / w^2) pins the 1/e^2 intensity convention, exp(-r^2 / w^2) pins 1/e, exp(-r^2 / (2 sigma^2)) pins the second-moment convention. Cross-check against the printed Rayleigh-range formula (pi w0^2/lambda pins 1/e^2). Token cues: '1/e^2', '4-sigma', 'd4sigma', 'ISO 11146', 'confocal parameter', 'beam diameter', 'FWHM spot'. A paper that prints both z_R = pi w0^2/lambda and b = 2 pi w0^2/lambda has declared the b = 2 z_R relation explicitly; a paper that prints only xi = L/b without defining b is unresolvable and should be tagged, not translated.

gaps.name: Pulse-duration parameterization and shape-dependent energy/peak-power/bandwidth factors
gaps.what_breaks: Same blindness as beam width but in the time axis, and worse because the shape-dependent numeric factors are load-bearing in formulas the tool would otherwise happily restore constants into. tau_FWHM, T0, the 1/e half-width, and the rms width are all dimension T. Dispersion length L_D = T0^2/|beta2|, soliton order N^2 = gamma P0 T0^2/|beta2|, soliton period z0 = (pi/2) L_D and the peak-power-from-energy relation all take the model parameter T0, not the measured FWHM, and the ratio between them depends on the assumed pulse shape. A dimensional linter that restores hbar and c into a soliton equation while T0 silently means tau_FWHM produces an answer wrong by a factor of three with no complaint.
gaps.magnitude: sech^2 intensity profile: tau_FWHM = 2 ln(1+sqrt(2)) T0 = 1.7627 T0, so substituting tau_FWHM for T0 inflates any T0^2 quantity (L_D, N^2, z0) by 1.7627^2 = 3.108. Gaussian (Agrawal's field convention A ~ exp(-t^2/(2 T0^2))): tau_FWHM = 2 sqrt(ln 2) T0 = 1.6651 T0, factor 2.773 in T0^2. Peak power from pulse energy: P0 = 0.9394 E/tau_FWHM for a Gaussian, P0 = 0.8814 E/tau_FWHM for sech^2 (6.6% apart, which matters for damage-threshold and B-integral claims). Time-bandwidth product: 0.4413 (Gaussian) vs 0.3148 (sech^2), a factor 1.402 in the inferred transform limit.
gaps.example: Dispersion length at 1550 nm, beta2 = -21.7 ps^2/km, measured 100 fs FWHM sech^2 pulse. Variant A (correct, T0 convention): T0 = 100 fs / 1.7627 = 56.7 fs, L_D = T0^2/|beta2| = (56.7e-3 ps)^2 / 21.7 ps^2/km = 148 m. Variant B (FWHM plugged in): L_D = (0.1 ps)^2/21.7 ps^2/km = 461 m. Both are dimensionally perfect; they differ by 3.11.
gaps.fingerprint: Look for the printed envelope: sech(t/T0) vs sech(1.7627 t/tau) vs exp(-t^2/(2 T0^2)) vs exp(-2 ln 2 t^2 / tau^2). Token cues: '1.76', '1.665', '0.315', '0.441', 'transform-limited', 'FWHM', 'HW1/e M', 'autocorrelation deconvolution factor' (1.543 for sech^2, 1.414 for Gaussian — that factor's presence itself declares the assumed shape). Also flag: whether the printed envelope is the field A or the intensity |A|^2, since exp(-t^2/(2T0^2)) as a field is exp(-t^2/T0^2) as an intensity.

gaps.name: Optical handedness labeling (IEEE/RF vs traditional-optics vs IAU) and the sign of Stokes V
gaps.what_breaks: The tool already carries a Fourier-sign flag and the engineering j = -i flag, but handedness is not derivable from the time convention: it is an independent community-set naming convention layered on top of it. The physical field is determined by the PRODUCT of the two flags, so a paper that states exp(+j omega t) and then imports 'RHCP' from optics literature describes a different field than either convention alone predicts. Downstream, the sign of Stokes V/S3 flips, the sigma+ / sigma- assignment to atomic transitions flips, the sign of measured circular dichroism and Faraday/magneto-optic rotation flips, and any Jones-to-Mueller translation inherits the flip. Nothing in the equation becomes dimensionally or even algebraically wrong — the labels are just attached to the other object.
gaps.magnitude: Exact sign flip on V (equivalently S3), and on the handedness label of every circular basis vector; combined with the time-convention flag it is a Z2 x Z2 structure of which only the product is physical. Astronomy adds a third variant: the IAU 1974 definition sets V = -S3 relative to the optics-style definition used in much of the polarimetry literature, so three-community papers can accumulate two independent flips (net zero) or one (net flip).
gaps.example: Same physical field, opposite labels. Traditional optics (observer looking INTO the oncoming beam; with exp(-i omega t), e_L = (x + i y)/sqrt(2) traces counterclockwise for the observer and is called LEFT circular): V = I_RCP - I_LCP in one common optics rendering. IEEE / RF / radio-astronomy: handedness by the right-hand rule with the thumb along k — the same physical field is called RIGHT circular, and the standard radio-astronomy Stokes definition V = I_LCP - I_RCP is written with the IEEE labels, so the two expressions in fact agree on the physical field and disagree on every label in them.
gaps.fingerprint: Explicit tokens: 'IEEE convention', 'IAU 1974', 'as seen by an observer looking toward the source', 'looking along the direction of propagation', 'from behind the transmitter'. Structural tests: does the paper print V = I_L - I_R or I_R - I_L; does it print e_pm = (x +- i y)/sqrt(2) together with a stated exp(-i omega t) or exp(+j omega t); is a magneto-optic/Faraday sign quoted against a stated B direction. Community priors are strong enough to use as weak evidence (antenna/radar/radio-astronomy -> IEEE; chiroptical spectroscopy and laser physics -> optics), but never as a substitute for the printed exponent.

gaps.name: The nonlinear-index symbol family: n2 [m^2/W] vs n2-bar [m^2/V^2] vs n2 [esu] vs gamma [1/(W m)]
gaps.what_breaks: A single symbol n2 carries three mutually incompatible dimensions across (and often within) papers, and the conversion edges between them are not unit conversions — they contain material parameters (n0, and for gamma the effective area A_eff and the wavelength). The tool's converter graph, as described, holds pure numeric/unit equivalences; it has no edge type for 'these two quantities are the same physical property expressed against a material-dependent normalization'. Consequences: (a) the solver will either silently accept whichever dimension makes the local equation balance, or (b) emit a false dimensional-inconsistency flag on a paper that legitimately uses Boyd's n2 and n2-bar in adjacent equations, and (c) an esu value has no recoverable dimension at all without knowing the definition it was measured against.
gaps.magnitude: n2[m^2/W] = (40 pi / c[m/s]) * n2[esu] / n0 = 4.19e-7 * n2[esu] / n0; equivalently n2[cm^2/W] = 4.19e-3 * n2[esu] / n0. (Derived: Gaussian I = (n0 c/4pi)<E^2> with c in cm/s and 1 W/m^2 = 1e3 erg/s/cm^2.) Check: fused silica n2 ~ 2.7e-20 m^2/W with n0 = 1.45 gives n2 ~ 0.9e-13 esu, matching the literature ~1e-13 esu. The n2 -> gamma edge: gamma = 2 pi n2 / (lambda A_eff); for SMF-28 (n2 = 2.6e-20 m^2/W, A_eff = 80 um^2, 1550 nm) gamma = 1.3 /(W km) — a number with different dimensions and a material-geometry factor of 1e12 m^-2 buried in it.
gaps.example: Variant A (intensity-referenced, SI): n = n0 + n2 I, [n2] = m^2/W. Variant B (field-referenced, SI, Boyd's n2-bar): n = n0 + (1/2) n2bar |E|^2, [n2bar] = m^2/V^2, with n2 = n2bar/(n0 eps0 c). Variant C (esu): n = n0 + n2 <E^2> with E in statvolt/cm. Variant D (fiber): the nonlinearity appears only as gamma in i gamma |A|^2 A, [gamma] = 1/(W m). A tool asked to 'restore constants' in Variant B without knowing which n2 it holds will produce Variant A's equation off by n0 eps0 c ~ 3.9e-3 S/m in a way that reads as a legitimate SI restoration.
gaps.fingerprint: Dimension of the printed coefficient is itself the discriminator when units are given — scan for m^2/W, cm^2/W, cm^2/statvolt^2, esu, W^-1 km^-1. Structural cues: a printed factor 1/2 in front of the nonlinear index term signals the field-referenced variant; the token 'esu' or an exponent near 1e-13 with no unit signals Gaussian; the presence of A_eff or 'effective area' signals the gamma variant; 'n2 (esu)' tables in older Chinese/Russian and pre-1990 US literature are near-universal.

gaps.name: Spectral-density and dispersion basis: per-wavelength vs per-frequency vs per-angular-frequency, with a NON-constant Jacobian (and the D vs beta2 sign flip)
gaps.what_breaks: The exclusion list covers per-Hz vs per-(rad/s), which is a constant Jacobian of 2 pi and therefore expressible as a rider. Per-wavelength vs per-frequency is structurally different: the Jacobian |dnu/dlambda| = c/lambda^2 is a FUNCTION of the spectral coordinate, so it cannot be a scalar rider and cannot be carried by the generator solve at all. Dimensional analysis does see that W/(m^2 nm) and W/(m^2 Hz) differ, but it cannot tell whether the author already applied the Jacobian, whether a 'peak' quoted in one basis was located in the other, or whether a density was converted by naively substituting nu = c/lambda. The same structure with one more derivative produces the fiber-optics dispersion pair D and beta2, where the Jacobian additionally carries a minus sign — the single most-tripped-over sign in fiber and ultrafast optics. Orthogonal to all of this is the energy-basis vs photon-basis choice (W vs photons/s), whose conversion factor h nu is also spectral-coordinate dependent.
gaps.magnitude: Jacobian c/lambda^2 = 1.25e14 Hz/m at 1550 nm (i.e. 1 nm = 125 GHz there, 1 nm = 375 GHz at 800 nm) — so the numeric factor changes by a factor of 3.7 across the common telecom/Ti:sapphire range and is not a constant at all. D <-> beta2: D = -(2 pi c / lambda^2) beta2, a SIGN FLIP plus 1.276 ps^2/km per ps/(nm km) at 1550 nm. Blackbody peak: lambda_max T = 2.898e-3 m K (per-lambda basis) but c/nu_max T = 5.10e-3 m K (per-nu basis) — the 'peak wavelength' differs by 1.76 depending on basis, with no error anywhere.
gaps.example: Standard SMF at 1550 nm, anomalous dispersion. Variant A (telecom/engineering, per-wavelength): D = +17 ps/(nm km), positive. Variant B (ultrafast/theory, per-angular-frequency): beta2 = -D lambda^2/(2 pi c) = -21.7 ps^2/km, negative. Both describe the same fiber; a tool that treats 'anomalous dispersion' as a sign-consistent tag, or converts by magnitude, will invert the sign of every soliton, modulation-instability, or chirp argument built on it.
gaps.fingerprint: Unit tokens are decisive when present: ps/(nm km) and ps^2/km, W/(m^2 nm) vs W/(m^2 Hz) vs W/(m^2 (rad/s)), photons/s/nm, 'per unit wavelength interval'. Prose tokens: 'anomalous'/'normal' dispersion together with a sign; 'dispersion slope' S = dD/dlambda (which relates to beta3 through TWO Jacobian terms: S = (2 pi c/lambda^2)^2 beta3 + (4 pi c/lambda^3) beta2, so a paper quoting only S and beta3 without the beta2 term has made a specific approximation). Any symbol whose units contain a spectral coordinate in the denominator should be forced to declare a basis before translation.

gaps.name: Amplitude-referenced vs power-referenced propagation/attenuation/gain constants (and the Neper's two dB values)
gaps.what_breaks: alpha, g, kappa, and the RF propagation constant gamma = alpha + j beta are all 1/length, and the exponential laws exp(-alpha z) applied to E and to I are both dimensionally perfect. Whether the coefficient is referenced to field amplitude or to power is a per-symbol convention that no dimensional check can see, and it multiplies against the already-covered decadic/Napierian fork to give four distinct combinations for what looks like one number. This is not the same object as a quantity-kind tag in the Gy/Sv sense: it does not change what is being measured, it changes the exponent by exactly 2 and propagates through every attenuation, gain, Q-factor, skin-depth, and loss-budget equation in the paper. It is also the origin of the 20-log vs 10-log split that makes 'refuse dB' insufficient — the tool must know the referencing to know which log rule the author used.
gaps.magnitude: Exactly 2 in the exponent coefficient: alpha_intensity = 2 alpha_field, e.g. alpha = 4 pi kappa / lambda (intensity) vs 2 pi kappa / lambda (field), for a complex index n + i kappa. In log units, 1 Np = 8.686 dB when the Neper is referenced to field amplitude (the SI/ISO definition: 20 log10 e), but 1 Np = 4.343 dB when someone treats alpha as a power coefficient. RF: gamma = alpha + j beta has alpha field-referenced by convention, so power decays as exp(-2 alpha z) — a loss budget computed as exp(-alpha z) in power is off by a factor 2 in the exponent, i.e. the loss in dB is halved.
gaps.example: Absorption of a medium with extinction coefficient kappa at wavelength lambda. Variant A (intensity/Beer-Lambert, standard in spectroscopy and NLO): I(z) = I0 exp(-alpha z), alpha = 4 pi kappa / lambda. Variant B (field, standard in waveguide and RF work): E(z) = E0 exp(-alpha z), alpha = 2 pi kappa / lambda, with power going as exp(-2 alpha z). At kappa = 1e-4 and lambda = 1550 nm, A gives alpha = 810 m^-1 and B gives 405 m^-1 for the same material.
gaps.fingerprint: Test what the exponential multiplies in the printed equation: E, A, a (field/envelope/mode amplitude) vs I, P, S (intensity/power/Poynting). Token cues: 'Np/m' or 'nepers' next to a propagation constant (almost always field-referenced); 'gamma = alpha + j beta'; 'amplitude gain coefficient'; a printed 8.686 or 4.343 or 0.4343 anywhere in the paper is a direct declaration of which referencing the author used; 20*log10 vs 10*log10 in the dB definition. In coupled-mode and NLS-type equations the envelope A is field-like even when normalized so |A|^2 is power — that mixed case (|A|^2 = power, but the loss term sits on A) is the most common source of the error and should be detected specifically.

gaps.name: Rabi frequency and light-matter coupling rate: Omega vs Omega/2, g vs the vacuum Rabi splitting 2g
gaps.what_breaks: The covered h-vs-hbar / nu-vs-omega / radian-collapse entry handles the 2 pi, but not the independent factor of 2 that comes from whether the Rabi frequency is defined as the coefficient in H = (hbar Omega/2) sigma_x or as the full coefficient of sigma_x, and whether a quoted 'vacuum Rabi frequency' is the coupling rate g or the observed splitting 2g. Both variants are pure numbers multiplying an already-dimensionally-correct energy, so the solve sees nothing. It compounds with the 2 pi: a quoted 'g = 10 MHz' can mean any of g/2pi = 10 MHz, g = 10e6 rad/s, or a splitting of 10 MHz, spanning a factor of 4 pi.
gaps.magnitude: Exactly 2 in Omega and in g, hence exactly 4 in the intensity or drive power required for a given pulse area, and exactly 4 in cooperativity C = g^2/(kappa gamma) if g is taken as the splitting. Compounded with a radian/cycle slip the spread reaches 4 pi ~ 12.6.
gaps.example: Two-level atom, dipole d, field amplitude E0, resonant drive. Variant A (most common, e.g. quantum-optics texts): Omega = d E0 / hbar, H_RWA = (hbar Omega/2)(sigma_+ + sigma_-), population inverted at pulse area integral Omega dt = pi. Variant B: Omega = d E0/(2 hbar), H_RWA = hbar Omega (sigma_+ + sigma_-), pi-pulse at integral 2 Omega dt = pi. Cavity QED: H = hbar g (a sigma_+ + h.c.) gives a normal-mode splitting of 2g, but 'vacuum Rabi frequency' is used in the literature for both g and 2g.
gaps.fingerprint: Read the printed Hamiltonian prefactor: hbar Omega/2 vs hbar Omega. Cross-check against the printed pi-pulse condition or the printed on-resonance excited-state population P_e = sin^2(Omega t/2) vs sin^2(Omega t). For cavity QED, check whether a quoted g is compared against a measured/plotted peak separation (splitting = 2g) or against kappa and gamma in a cooperativity formula (coupling rate). Token cues: 'vacuum Rabi splitting', 'normal-mode splitting', 'pulse area', 'g/2pi'.

gaps.name: Phase-noise script-L(f) = (1/2) S_phi(f), and its small-angle validity boundary
gaps.what_breaks: This is a factor of 2 between two spectral quantities that is NOT the one-sided/two-sided PSD fork already excluded: script-L was historically defined as the ratio of single-sideband noise power in a 1 Hz band to total carrier power, and IEEE Std 1139 redefined it as exactly half the one-sided phase-fluctuation PSD S_phi. The two coincide only in the small-angle limit; when the integrated phase fluctuation approaches or exceeds 1 rad the original definition is bounded and the IEEE one is not, so script-L can legitimately exceed 0 dBc/Hz. A converter that treats the 1/2 as an unconditional rider will produce nonsense in exactly the near-carrier region where oscillator papers live. Additionally, S_phi and the fractional-frequency PSD S_y are related by a frequency-dependent factor, S_phi(f) = (nu0^2/f^2) S_y(f), which is another non-constant Jacobian rather than a scalar.
gaps.magnitude: Exactly 2 (3.01 dB) between script-L and S_phi. The S_phi <-> S_y edge carries nu0^2/f^2, spanning many orders of magnitude across a typical 1 Hz - 10 MHz offset sweep, and the S_phi <-> S_x (time) edge carries (2 pi nu0)^2.
gaps.example: An oscillator with S_phi(10 kHz) = 2e-13 rad^2/Hz. Variant A (IEEE 1139): script-L(10 kHz) = 1e-13 /Hz = -130 dBc/Hz. Variant B (pre-1988 literal SSB-power definition, and many instrument manuals): script-L is quoted directly as the measured SSB-to-carrier ratio, which equals A only under small-angle conditions. A paper predating 1988, or one quoting a measured spectrum-analyzer trace, must be tagged rather than converted.
gaps.fingerprint: Tokens 'dBc/Hz', 'script L(f)', 'SSB phase noise', 'IEEE 1139', 'rad^2/Hz'. Structural: whether the paper prints script-L = S_phi/2 explicitly; whether a quoted script-L exceeds 0 dBc/Hz (which is only possible under the IEEE definition and is a positive identification); whether the paper works in S_y and Allan variance (time-and-frequency-metrology dialect) or in dBc/Hz (RF-instrument dialect).

gaps.name: Power-wave (Kurokawa) vs pseudo-wave S-parameters at complex reference impedance
gaps.what_breaks: For real Z0 the two wave normalizations agree and nothing is at stake, which is why this never surfaces in textbook problems. For complex Z0 (on-wafer transistor characterization, lossy-line de-embedding) they differ: the reflection coefficient is (Z - Z0*)/(Z + Z0) under power waves and (Z - Z0)/(Z + Z0) under traveling/pseudo waves, so conjugate match gives Gamma = 0 in one and a nonzero Gamma in the other, and |S21|^2 means transducer gain in one normalization and something else in the other. I list it for boundary honesty: it is a genuine, daily trap for microwave engineers, but it is a linear-algebra normalization on a scattering matrix rather than a units or dimensional convention, and a tool aimed at theoretical-physics reading will essentially never meet it.
gaps.magnitude: Zero for real Z0; for complex Z0 it changes Gamma by the conjugation of Z0 in the numerator, which for a typical on-wafer Z0 = 50 - j5 ohm shifts inferred reflection by order 10% in magnitude and several degrees in phase, and can move a stability-circle conclusion.
gaps.example: Variant A (Kurokawa power waves): a = (V + Z0 I)/(2 sqrt(Re Z0)), b = (V - Z0* I)/(2 sqrt(Re Z0)), Gamma_in = (Z - Z0*)/(Z + Z0). Variant B (traveling/pseudo waves): a = (V + Z0 I)/(2 sqrt(|Re Z0|)) with b = (V - Z0 I)/(...), Gamma_in = (Z - Z0)/(Z + Z0).
gaps.fingerprint: Tokens 'power waves', 'Kurokawa', 'pseudo-waves', 'complex reference impedance', 'renormalization of S-parameters'; any appearance of Z0* in a printed definition. Presence of a purely real stated Z0 (50 or 75 ohm) makes the fork inert and it can be ignored.

found.overall:
Optics/photonics/RF is only partly covered by the existing lists. The E&M rider system, the 4-pi rationalization, decadic/Napierian, the Fourier/analytic-signal cluster, and the chi^(n) degeneracy factors take out a large fraction of the classic NLO traps, and I deliberately did not resubmit them. What remains falls into three structural families that the current architecture cannot express, and I think those families matter more than any individual entry:

(1) DIMENSION-NEUTRAL PARAMETERIZATION. Beam widths, pulse durations, and Rayleigh-vs-confocal lengths are all lengths and times. The generator solve is structurally blind to them, yet they are where experimental photonics papers actually go wrong, and the errors (2, 4, 3.11, 1.39) are the same size as the 4-pi and factor-2 errors the tool already exists to catch. The right fix is a per-symbol parameterization tag (shape x fraction-threshold x radius-or-diameter x field-or-intensity) with a converter table, harvested from the envelope the paper actually prints rather than from prose. This machinery would also cover cases outside my field (rms vs FWHM widths generally).

(2) NON-CONSTANT JACOBIANS. The exclusion list's per-Hz vs per-(rad/s) fork is a constant, so it fits the rider architecture. Per-wavelength vs per-frequency does not — the factor c/lambda^2 depends on the spectral coordinate, changes by 3.7x across the wavelengths I read about daily, and produces the D-vs-beta2 sign flip and the two different blackbody peaks. Similarly S_phi <-> S_y carries nu0^2/f^2, and energy-basis <-> photon-basis carries h*nu. Any symbol whose units contain a coordinate in the denominator needs a declared basis and a Jacobian-carrying edge type, not a rider.

(3) MATERIAL-PARAMETERIZED CONVERTER EDGES. n2 in m^2/W, n2-bar in m^2/V^2, n2 in esu, and gamma in 1/(W m) are the same physical property under four normalizations whose conversions contain n0, eps0, c, lambda, and A_eff. The converter graph as described holds unit equivalences; it needs an edge class that can be instantiated only after material parameters are supplied, and should refuse (not guess) when they are not. Note I corrected my own remembered constant here: the right factor is n2[m^2/W] = 4.19e-7 * n2[esu]/n0, verified both by derivation from I = (n0 c/4pi)<E^2> and against fused silica (2.7e-20 m^2/W <-> ~1e-13 esu).

The handedness entry is different in kind and worth flagging separately: it is the first case I have seen in this list where two convention flags are individually meaningless and only their product is physical. The tool should be able to express 'this axis is not independent — resolve it jointly with the time convention', because a paper stating exp(+j omega t) and importing optics handedness labels is internally inconsistent in a way that is worth reporting rather than silently normalizing.

Two things I checked and decided NOT to submit, for the record: the d_il contracted-notation factor 2 on off-diagonal elements is the same structure as the Voigt gamma = 2 epsilon entry already excluded (the fix is to extend that rider to the nonlinear d-matrix, not a new gap), and the rms-vs-peak phasor amplitude in RF is close enough to the excluded analytic-signal factor 2 that I treat it as covered.

verdict.lens: Nonlinear optics / ultrafast photonics / fiber optics / RF-microwave engineering

verdicts.gap: Transverse beam-size parameterization (spot size, radius vs diameter, Rayleigh range vs confocal parameter)
verdicts.notes: Recomputed all factors. I=I0exp(-2r^2/w^2) vs exp(-r^2/w'^2) gives w'=w/sqrt2, so reusing one numeric value across the two peak-intensity formulas (2P/(pi w^2) vs P/(pi w^2)) is exactly 2. FWHM: 2r^2/w^2=ln2 -> FWHM=w*sqrt(2 ln2)=1.1774w, squared 1.386. d4sigma=2w for a Gaussian (ISO 11146). Boyd & Kleinman JAP 39, 3597 (1968): xi=L/b with b=2z_R, xi_opt=2.84 -> L/z_R=5.68; misreading b as z_R halves L or doubles w0^2, as claimed. One redundancy: 'w at 1/e of field' and 'w at 1/e^2 of intensity' are the same radius, not two candidates (harmless, but the tag's enumeration should not double-count them). Not in coverage (nothing in the 113 systems or the 21-fork registry touches beam parameterization) and not in exclusions: the excluded quantity-kind tag (Gy vs Sv) separates non-interconvertible kinds, whereas this needs interconvertible variants of one quantity carrying numeric factors, so schema_feature/v1 is the right slot.

verdicts.gap: Pulse-duration parameterization and shape-dependent energy/peak-power/bandwidth factors
verdicts.notes: Every number recomputed and correct. sech^2: FWHM=2*arccosh(sqrt2)*T0=2 ln(1+sqrt2) T0=1.7627 T0, squared 3.108. Gaussian |A|^2=exp(-t^2/T0^2): FWHM=2 sqrt(ln2) T0=1.6651 T0, squared 2.773. Energy: Gaussian E=P0 T0 sqrt(pi) -> P0=0.9394 E/tau; sech^2 E=2 P0 T0 -> P0=0.8814 E/tau; ratio 1.0658 (6.6%). TBP 0.4413 vs 0.3148, ratio 1.402. Autocorrelation deconvolution 1.543 (sech^2) / 1.414 (Gaussian) correct. L_D example verified: T0=56.7 fs -> 148 m vs 461 m with beta2=-21.7 ps^2/km. Real and uncovered. Scoping note: this is not a second build item — it is the same per-symbol parameterization tag as the beam-width entry (shape x threshold x field-or-intensity), instantiated on the time axis; ship them as one schema feature with two symbol families.

verdicts.gap: Optical handedness labeling (IEEE/RF vs traditional-optics vs IAU) and the sign of Stokes V
verdicts.notes: Structure verified by direct computation: with exp(-i omega t), (x+iy)/sqrt2 gives E=(cos wt, sin wt), which is counterclockwise to an observer facing the beam (optics: LEFT) and right-handed by the thumb-along-k rule (IEEE: RIGHT). So the same field carries opposite labels, exactly as claimed, and this is independent of the already-covered Fourier-sign / j=-i flags. CORRECTION to the example: the IAU 1974 standard is V = RCP - LCP with IEEE handedness (positive V = IEEE right-handed), not 'V = I_LCP - I_RCP'. V = LCP - RCP is a widespread deviation (much pulsar/VLBI literature), not the standard, and as written the entry's IAU sentence and its radio-astronomy sentence contradict each other. Both are documented in the literature, which if anything strengthens the case: the fork is three-valued (optics label, IAU/IEEE label, LCP-RCP deviants) and must be resolved from the printed definition, never from community prior. Slotting: this is an entry on the existing round-2 sign-convention axis plus a genuinely new 'dependent flag, resolve jointly with the time convention' feature, rather than a free-standing axis.

verdicts.gap: The nonlinear-index symbol family: n2 [m^2/W] vs n2-bar [m^2/V^2] vs n2 [esu] vs gamma [1/(W m)]
verdicts.notes: Conversion re-derived independently and the critic's self-correction is right: from I=(n0 c/4pi)<E^2> (cgs) and 1 W/cm^2 = 1e7 erg/s/cm^2, n2[cm^2/W] = 4pi*1e7/(n0 c[cm/s]) * n2[esu] = 4.19e-3 n2[esu]/n0, i.e. n2[m^2/W] = (40pi/c[m/s]) n2[esu]/n0 = 4.19e-7 n2[esu]/n0. Fused-silica check: 2.7e-20 m^2/W, n0=1.45 -> 9.3e-14 esu, matching the quoted ~1e-13. Boyd's n2 = n2bar/(n0 eps0 c) confirmed from I=(1/2)eps0 n0 c|E|^2 with Delta n=(1/2)n2bar|E|^2. gamma check: 2pi(2.6e-20)/(1.55e-6 * 80e-12) = 1.32 /(W km). Minor unit correction: n0 eps0 c ~ 3.85e-3 SIEMENS (eps0 c = 1/377 ohm^-1), not S/m. Partial-credit caveat on the architecture claim: the excluded quantity-kind entry chi_v/chi_mol/chi_g already implies a material-parameterized relation (density, molar mass), so 'the converter graph needs an edge class instantiable only after material parameters are supplied' is half-anticipated. The new content is the specific four-node n2 table plus the point that the esu node has no recoverable dimension without its defining equation, which the chi entry does not cover.

verdicts.gap: Spectral-density and dispersion basis: per-wavelength vs per-frequency vs per-angular-frequency, with a NON-constant Jacobian (and the D vs beta2 sign flip)
verdicts.notes: Core claim survives and is the strongest architectural entry here: the excluded per-Hz vs per-(rad/s) fork is a constant 2pi and fits a rider; |dnu/dlambda|=c/lambda^2 does not. Verified: D = -(2pi c/lambda^2) beta2 gives 1.275 ps^2/km per ps/(nm km) at 1550 nm and -21.7 ps^2/km for D=+17, sign flip included. Slope relation re-derived: dD/dlambda = (4pi c/lambda^3)beta2 + (2pi c/lambda^2)^2 beta3, exactly as printed. Blackbody 2.898e-3 vs 5.10e-3 m K, ratio 1.76, correct. TWO numeric corrections: (i) c/lambda^2 at 1550 nm is 1.25e20 Hz/m, not 1.25e14 Hz/m (the derived 125 GHz per nm is right; the unit label is off by 1e6 — 1.25e14 is Hz/um); (ii) at 800 nm it is c*1nm/lambda^2 = 469 GHz/nm, not 375 GHz (375 GHz corresponds to ~894 nm). The stated 3.7x spread across 800-1550 nm is right since (1550/800)^2=3.75.

verdicts.gap: Amplitude-referenced vs power-referenced propagation/attenuation/gain constants (and the Neper's two dB values)
verdicts.notes: Physics verified and uncovered: alpha_I = 2 alpha_E; alpha=4pi kappa/lambda vs 2pi kappa/lambda gives 811 vs 405 m^-1 at kappa=1e-4, 1550 nm (recomputed); 1 Np = 20 log10 e = 8.686 dB for an amplitude ratio, 10 log10 e = 4.343 dB if alpha is mistakenly read as a power coefficient; RF gamma=alpha+j beta is field-referenced so power goes as exp(-2 alpha z). Distinct from the covered decadic/Napierian fork, which it multiplies. Mis-slotted, though: 'new_axis' implies a document-level convention state, and referencing is NOT document-level — one paper routinely carries a field-referenced waveguide loss alpha alongside an intensity-referenced Beer-Lambert alpha or a power gain g, which is precisely the mixed NLS case the entry itself flags (|A|^2 = power but the loss sits on A). It belongs as the field-or-intensity slot of the per-symbol parameterization tag proposed in the beam-width entry, harvested from what the printed exponential multiplies, not as a span-scoped axis.

verdicts.gap: Rabi frequency and light-matter coupling rate: Omega vs Omega/2, g vs the vacuum Rabi splitting 2g
verdicts.notes: Real and not in the registry: the covered h-vs-hbar / nu-vs-omega entry supplies the 2pi only. H=(hbar Omega/2)sigma_x vs hbar Omega sigma_x is exactly 2 in Omega, hence 4 in drive intensity for a fixed pulse area; H=hbar g(a sigma_+ + h.c.) gives normal-mode splitting 2g and 'vacuum Rabi frequency' is used in the literature for both g and 2g. Two caveats. (i) Provenance overlap: one common route to the Omega vs Omega/2 slip is the field-amplitude convention (E0 cos wt vs (1/2)E0 e^{-iwt}+c.c.), which IS the excluded analytic-signal factor 2; the new content is specifically the Hamiltonian prefactor and the g-vs-2g splitting, and the entry should be written so it does not re-litigate the amplitude convention. (ii) The 'exactly 4 in cooperativity' line presumes one C definition — C = g^2/(kappa gamma), C = g^2/(2 kappa gamma) and C = 4g^2/(kappa gamma) all circulate, so C carries its own factor fork on top. registry_entry / v2 is the right slot and tier.

verdicts.gap: Phase-noise script-L(f) = (1/2) S_phi(f), and its small-angle validity boundary
verdicts.notes: Source-checked: IEEE Std 1139 (1988, carried into later revisions) defines script-L(f) as one half the spectral density of phase fluctuations, superseding the earlier literal SSB-power-ratio definition, and the two agree only in the small-angle regime — so script-L > 0 dBc/Hz is possible under the IEEE definition and impossible under the original, which is a valid positive identification. Arithmetic checks: S_phi=2e-13 rad^2/Hz -> script-L=1e-13/Hz=-130 dBc/Hz; S_phi=(nu0^2/f^2)S_y and S_phi=(2 pi nu0)^2 S_x both correct, and the first is a second genuine non-constant-Jacobian edge. Distinct from the excluded one-sided/two-sided fork (the two factors of 2 can appear together and cancel, which is exactly why the field is confused). Scope caveat, matching the entry's own 'likely' confidence: this is RF/time-frequency-metrology dialect, far rarer in the theoretical-physics reading the tool targets than the entry's neighbours, so v2 is right and it should sit near the bottom of that tier.

verdicts.gap: Power-wave (Kurokawa) vs pseudo-wave S-parameters at complex reference impedance
verdicts.notes: Verified correct and correctly self-excluded — no action. Kurokawa (1965) power waves a=(V+Z0 I)/(2 sqrt(Re Z0)), b=(V-Z0* I)/(2 sqrt(Re Z0)) give Gamma=(Z-Z0*)/(Z+Z0); traveling/pseudo waves (Marks & Williams) give (Z-Z0)/(Z+Z0); the two numerators differ by Z0-Z0*=2j Im Z0, so for Z0=50-j5 near a match the absolute shift in Gamma is ~10/100 = 0.1, consistent with the stated order-10% claim, and it is identically zero for real Z0. But it is a scattering-matrix normalization, not a units or dimensional convention, and carries no dimensionful content the generator solve could act on, so tier out_of_scope is the correct disposition: record it in the boundary/out-of-scope note, do not open a registry row.

verdict.overall: All nine claims are physically real; I recomputed every stated number and found the lens unusually reliable — the two flagged self-corrections (n2 esu factor, Boyd-Kleinman b=2z_R) are both right. Three numeric/attribution corrections are needed inside otherwise-sound entries: (1) c/lambda^2 at 1550 nm is 1.25e20 Hz/m, not 1.25e14 (the 125 GHz/nm derived from it is correct), and the 800 nm figure is 469 GHz/nm, not 375; (2) n0 eps0 c is ~3.9e-3 siemens, not S/m; (3) the IAU 1974 standard is V = RCP - LCP with IEEE handedness — 'V = I_LCP - I_RCP' is a widespread deviation rather than the radio-astronomy standard, and as written that entry's IAU and radio sentences contradict each other. One entry is mis-slotted: amplitude-vs-power referencing is a per-symbol tag, not a document-level axis, because a single paper mixes field-referenced waveguide loss with intensity-referenced Beer-Lambert absorption; it should be the field-or-intensity slot of the same parameterization tag the beam-width entry proposes. Two further scoping calls: the beam-width and pulse-duration entries are one schema feature with two symbol families, not two builds; and the 'converter graph needs material-parameterized edges' architecture claim is half-anticipated by the excluded chi_v/chi_mol/chi_g quantity-kind entry, so the n2 entry's real yield is the four-node table (and the fact that an esu value has no recoverable dimension without its defining equation) rather than a new edge class. Net: the strongest genuinely new architecture is (a) the per-symbol parameterization/referencing tag harvested from printed envelopes and exponentials, which is dimension-neutral and therefore structurally invisible to the generator solve, and (b) the non-constant-Jacobian edge class (per-lambda vs per-nu, D vs beta2, S_phi vs S_y, energy vs photon basis), which is correctly distinguished from the constant-2pi rider already excluded. The handedness entry's dependent-flag observation — two individually meaningless flags whose product is physical — is a real structural addition to the existing sign axis and is worth taking seriously beyond its optics instance."
